1 1 . This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') has been filed against award dated 19/04/2017 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur,
District - Surguja (CG) in Motor Accident Claim No.188/2016.
2.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur,
District - Surguja
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By the impugned award, learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.7,79,000/- in favour of the claimants as compensation on account of death of Mahesh Kumar Prajapati in an unfortunate accident that took place on 10/12/2015 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle (Bus) bearing registration No.CG-15/A.B-1179.
A claim application claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.27,00,000/- was filed by the claimants which was resisted by the respondents - driver, owner and insurance company.

Learned Tribunal, after framing issues, decided the same in favour of the claimants and awarded compensation as stated above and the driver, owner and the insurance company were jointly held liable to pay the compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant / claimant submits that the finding recorded by the learned Tribunal is bad in law.
The monthly income has been wrongly assessed by the learned Tribunal and compensation on other heads is also on the lower side.
Therefore, the finding is perverse and is liable to be set aside.
4. Learned counsel for respondents 1, 2 and 3 support the award.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the records.

6. Looking to the evidence available and also taking guidance from the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009)
6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi and ors, (2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., (2018) 18 SCC 130, this Court hereby computes the compensation in the following manner - 1 Monthly income Rs.6000/-
2 Future Prospects 40% Rs.8400/-
(6000+2400) 3 Yearly income (8400x12) Rs.1,00,800/-
4  deduction for personal exp. Rs.50400/-
(100800 / 2) 5 Applying Multiplier of 18 Rs.9,07,200/-
6.

7. Filial Consortium + Rs.1,60,000/-
TOTAL COMPENSATION Rs.10,97,200/-
7.
The learned Tribunal awarded Rs.7,79,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation now assessed and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.3,18,200/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim application to be deposited within a period of 60 days.
After deposit, Rs.50,000/- each shall be paid to appellant No.3 and 4.
Rs. 1 lakh shall be invested in a nationalised bank as fixed deposit in the name of appellant No.1 and 2 for two years.
Remaining amount shall be paid to appellant No.2 through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
8. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed.

Sd/-
